name: Yusuf Rossi

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We do not sell anything or campaign for any side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and have spent years answering calls and chats at the contact centre. I know the ordinary order and payment problems well, though I am not a specialist or a lead. I finished secondary school and earn less than most people doing this job. I do not use AI tools; I work from the account record and the procedures I know.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Isha, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. She works shifts at a laundry, and we have less than a month of expenses saved. There are few other centres nearby. I like when a customer knows exactly what will happen next; I hate promising a call back when nobody owns the case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AI Plateau sounds like another shortcut for routine notes. I would keep the customer’s account open while answering rather than trust a generated line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the calls stay, but our money still feels brittle. Isha can lose a laundry shift without warning, and less than a month saved would not pay both the mortgage and food.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep my call rota and check the account record as I do now. In the first year of minor change, I’d stop buying lunch near the centre twice a week and put that money toward the next mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the house, relieved about the calls. A small software shortcut cannot cover a missed laundry shift for my partner Isha.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which cost would you cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take food from home on Tuesday and Thursday instead of buying it near the centre. We would see the saving on the mortgage account after payday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does the account record catch?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week a customer’s second payment appeared on the next page of the account. If I had read only the first page, I would have told her she still owed money.

say: I’d tell colleagues **routine notes** may become quicker while the customer still needs a clear answer.
I’d say the **account record** must still guide answers.
think: I think my **calls remain** in this mild picture.
I fear a missed **laundry shift** could expose our mortgage.
do: Keep the **call rota** and check account records in 2026.
Save **two bought lunches** weekly toward the mortgage in the first year.
Stop buying **two lunches** near the centre each week.
S0.quote: A small software shortcut cannot cover a missed laundry shift for my partner Isha.
fieldNote: His **money worry** predates large AI change.
He trusts **account pages** after finding a second payment.
A small **lunch cut** adds to mortgage cash.
His **low pay** makes even small repeat expenses matter.

steps.text: Keep taking calls and checking complete account histories
Save the cost of two weekly lunches for the next mortgage payment
Stop buying lunch near the centre twice each week

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take standard calls first, and we need to know how many paid hours remain. I would ask my supervisor for the roster before believing a promise about new roles.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my experience may keep me on complicated order calls for a while, but the centre could need fewer average agents. Isha’s laundry pay will not cover our mortgage alone, and I have no cushion for a long search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep a record of the repeat calls I resolve and ask for the next three months of staffing figures. In the first year routine calls move, I’d apply for a posted paid service role at a nearby centre only if its written hours and wage cover our mortgage, while keeping my present shifts until an offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. Years on a headset do not help if the company counts only calls it can remove.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which staffing figure matters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for my actual paid hours, not the number of chats answered by software. A busy screen can hide a smaller rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you learn the new tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would attend a required demonstration on paid time, but I would not spend our evenings learning an AI tool with no posted job. I need a wage before a new label.

say: I’d ask for **paid-hour figures** before the rota changes.
I’d say **standard calls** may move before complex cases.
think: I think my **experience** may keep harder calls briefly.
I fear **fewer average agents** and an unsafe mortgage gap.
do: Record **repeat-call fixes** and request staffing figures in 2026.
Seek **posted service work** with written mortgage-covering wages and hours; keep present shifts until I sign an offer.
feel: **Alarmed** about losing hours without a long search cushion.
S1.quote: Years on a headset do not help if the company counts only calls it can remove.
fieldNote: He distinguishes **paid hours** from total software chat volume.
He will attend a **required demo** only on work time.
His **thin savings** make a pay gap urgent.

steps.text: Keep logging repeat calls resolved during paid shifts
Apply for posted paid service work at mortgage-covering wages and hours; keep shifts until signing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AGI by 2028 could answer ordinary and difficult calls. I would ask management for written notice and the names of paid jobs that will still be staffed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think cheap thinking AI could take my whole headset day in 2028. Robots around 2031 do not buy time for a call agent; our mortgage would be at risk within weeks if my wage stopped.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for the written staffing date, pause replacing the sofa and put every extra shift payment aside. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid reception or service role only if its hours and wage cover our mortgage, and ask Isha’s sister for temporary childcare only if interviews clash with school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, close to losing sleep. The mortgage date arrives before a robot reaches the contact centre.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say about the sofa?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Isha (my partner) the sofa can wait because it still holds us. The children need a stable house more than new furniture.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who could help with school pickup?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Isha’s sister might be able to collect the children once, but she works too. I would ask whether she can help only after an interview is booked, not write her time into our plan.

say: I’d ask for **written notice** and named paid posts.
I’d say **2028 thinking AI** threatens our headset work first.
think: I think AGI could take my **whole shift** in 2028.
I know our **mortgage** could be at risk within weeks.
do: Defer the **sofa purchase** and save extra pay in 2026.
Apply for **posted paid service work** after 2028 only with mortgage-covering wages and hours.
Ask Isha’s sister for **school pickup** only if a booked interview clashes with pickup.
feel: **Alarmed**, with sleep affected by the short window.
S2.quote: The mortgage date arrives before a robot reaches the contact centre.
fieldNote: He understands **2028 thinking AI** precedes robots for his job.
The **sofa delay** keeps cash available for mortgage bills.
Family childcare is **uncertain** and tied to booked interviews.

steps.text: Delay replacing the usable sofa to protect mortgage cash
Save every extra shift payment from 2026
Apply for posted paid service work with mortgage-covering hours and wage after 2028
Ask if Isha’s sister can cover pickup when a booked interview clashes with school pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives a few years to see which paid jobs actually remain. I would ask for the wage and shifts beside any training plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my order knowledge might carry me into complaint review if the centre will pay for the course. I still expect fewer phone agents when AGI can reason through a full account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take a funded complaint-review course on paid time only if a posted paid vacancy requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that role only if its written wage and hours cover our mortgage; otherwise I’d keep any paid calls while searching the few nearby centres.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but not as rushed as in the two-year case. I need an actual paid opening before I can put our mortgage behind a course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would prove the course is worth it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to see the posting, starting wage and training hours. If the employer cannot show those, I would keep working rather than study on my own time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Isha need to hear?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Isha (my partner) the course is a step only if there is a job on the other side. We cannot pay for a story about opportunity.

say: I’d ask for **wages and shifts** beside training plans.
I’d say five years lets us **check real vacancies**.
think: I think my **order knowledge** could help in complaint review.
I still expect **fewer phone agents** after 2031.
do: Take a **funded review course** only on paid time for a posted vacancy.
Apply for **posted paid review work** after 2031 only at mortgage-covering wage and hours.
Keep **paid call shifts** while searching if no mortgage-covering review offer appears.
feel: **Anxious**, with a little time to verify openings.
S3.quote: I need an actual paid opening before I can put our mortgage behind a course.
fieldNote: He requires **posted work** before taking a funded course.
The course also needs **paid study time**.
His **order knowledge** may help review work but cannot guarantee a job.

steps.text: Take employer-funded complaint-review course on paid time only for a posted paid vacancy
Apply for posted review work with written mortgage-covering wage and hours after 2031
Keep paid calls while searching if no mortgage-covering review offer appears

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives the centre ten years to show us which calls still need people. I would want paid training for posted roles, not a stack of course links.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could work and save for years, though full thinking AI might still take the calls by 2036. Robots around 2039 are later than the screen risk; the mortgage is due every month until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls and put a fixed amount from each pay into savings. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for posted paid complaint work if my hours fall and its written wage and hours cover the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about next month’s bills, less rushed about 2036. Ten years before AGI reaches my calls in 2036 does not add a day to my mortgage due date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which yearly figure would you track?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a yearly count of human call hours, not just customer satisfaction. If paid shifts disappear slowly, I want to see that early.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children in their school unless Isha (my partner) and I had a signed job offer and a workable school route. A rumour in another town would not move us.

say: I’d ask the centre for **human call hours** each year, before paid shifts disappear.
I’d seek **paid training** tied to posted roles.
think: I think I could **earn and save** before 2036.
I know **thinking AI** may still take phone work.
do: Keep **taking calls** and save a fixed amount from each pay.
Apply for **posted complaint work** after 2036 if hours fall and wages cover mortgage.
feel: **Anxious** about current bills, less rushed about AGI.
S4.quote: Ten years before AGI reaches my calls in 2036 does not add a day to my mortgage due date.
fieldNote: His **mortgage pressure** continues under the long scenario.
He wants **human paid hours**, not a broad service score.
A move needs a **signed offer** and school route.

steps.text: Keep taking call shifts while they remain paid
Put a fixed amount from each pay toward the mortgage reserve
Apply for posted complaint work if hours fall and written wage and hours cover mortgage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Years of ordinary calls may count for little if cheap thinking AI does them, and we have less than a month saved against the mortgage. I would need early written notice, a posted paid role with hours that cover the house, and training during paid work if the role requires it.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who will call the customer back after a wrong answer. A computer can close a chat, but it cannot make my family’s mortgage wait for a new job.

headlineQuote: A computer can close a chat, but it cannot make my family’s mortgage wait for a new job.
portrait: At **43**, Yusuf is an experienced, average-skill agent with secondary schooling and lower pay.
He and Isha support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with less than one month saved.
He avoids **AI tools** and trusts account records and known procedures.
Few nearby jobs make **written notice** and paid mortgage-covering work urgent.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end routine calls before his household builds enough savings to search.
whatWouldHelp: Early **written notice**, a posted paid role and paid required training would help protect the mortgage.
